title: Frontend Interview Questions & Answers
source: PhonePe, Myntra & General React Interview Experiences (LinkedIn)

questions.question: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
questions.answer: Track the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit possible.
questions.tip: Always mention brute force O(n²) first, then optimize to O(n).

questions.question: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.answer: Sliding window with a Map to track characters and their latest index.

questions.question: Two Sum - Sorted Array (Two Pointer)
questions.answer: Use two pointers from both ends. Move left pointer if sum is too small, right pointer if too large.
questions.tip: Only works because the array is sorted.

questions.question: Flatten a deeply nested array without using flat()
questions.answer: Use recursion with reduce, or an iterative stack-based approach.

questions.question: First non-repeating character in a string (O(n) solution)
questions.answer: Two-pass approach: build frequency map, then find first char with frequency 1.

questions.question: Merge K sorted linked lists
questions.answer: Use divide-and-conquer: repeatedly merge pairs of lists until one remains. Alternatively use a min-heap.

complexity.time: O(N log k) where N = total nodes, k = number of lists

questions.tip: Explain time/space complexity without being asked.

questions.question: Lowest Common Ancestor in a Binary Tree
questions.answer: Recursively search left and right subtrees. If both return non-null, current node is the LCA.

questions.question: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.answer: Use a monotonic deque (decreasing order of values) to track the max in the current window.

questions.question: Classic var + setTimeout closure trap: what does this print and why?
questions.answer: Prints '3 3 3'. var is function-scoped, so all three callbacks share the same 'i' variable. By the time the timeouts fire, the loop has finished and i = 3.
questions.tip: Explain the event loop too: setTimeout callbacks run after the synchronous loop finishes.

questions.question: Write debounce from scratch, no libraries
questions.answer: Debounce waits until the user stops calling the function for a given delay, then fires once.
key_points: Debounce waits until user STOPS calling the function
Throttle limits to once per interval (different concept)
apply(this, args) preserves context - important for methods
clearTimeout on each call resets the timer

questions.question: Write throttle from scratch, return the last call result
questions.answer: Throttle limits function execution to once per time interval. Use timestamp comparison.
questions.tip: Use throttle for scroll/resize events, debounce for search inputs.

questions.question: Write Promise.all polyfill
questions.answer: Promise.all resolves when ALL promises resolve (preserving order), and rejects immediately on the first rejection.
questions.tip: Also mention Promise.allSettled (waits for all, doesn't short-circuit) and Promise.race (first to settle wins).

questions.question: Explain the event loop with a real example
questions.answer: JavaScript is single-threaded. The event loop processes the call stack first, then microtasks (Promises), then macrotasks (setTimeout).
key_points: Microtask queue - Promises, queueMicrotask (drains completely before next macrotask)
Macrotask queue - setTimeout, setInterval, DOM events

questions.question: Write a custom event emitter with on(), off(), emit()
questions.answer: Implement a pub/sub pattern with an events map storing arrays of listener functions.

questions.question: Promises vs Async/Await with an API call example
questions.answer: Async/Await is syntactic sugar over Promises. Same microtask queue behavior, but async/await is easier to read and debug.

questions.question: `this` keyword in objects, normal functions, and arrow functions
questions.answer: Normal functions have dynamic `this` (depends on caller). Arrow functions inherit `this` lexically from surrounding scope. Object methods use the object before the dot as `this`.
questions.tip: Common mistake: passing an object method as a callback loses 'this'. Fix: use .bind(this) or wrap in an arrow function.

questions.question: Deep Copy vs Shallow Copy
questions.answer: Shallow copy copies top-level properties but nested objects still share references. Deep copy creates a fully independent clone at all levels.

questions.question: JWT Authentication - where should tokens be stored in the browser?
questions.answer: Best practice is HttpOnly cookies. localStorage is XSS-vulnerable. HttpOnly cookies can't be read by JS.

options.localStorage: Persistent, but vulnerable to XSS - JS can read it
options.sessionStorage: Cleared on tab close, still XSS-vulnerable
options.httpOnlyCookie: JS cannot access it, safe from XSS. Mitigate CSRF with SameSite=Strict + CSRF tokens

questions.recommendation: Store JWT in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie. For SPAs: short-lived access tokens in memory + refresh tokens in HttpOnly cookies.
questions.tip: PhonePe is a payments app - expect this question. Show you understand why cookie > localStorage.

questions.question: ES6+ features used in modern JavaScript
questions.answer: Key features: let/const, arrow functions, template literals, destructuring, rest/spread, default params, optional chaining (?.), nullish coalescing (??), Promise, async/await, modules (import/export), Map, Set, Symbol, class syntax, Array.from(), Object.entries().
questions.tip: Pick 3-4 and give a concrete use-case for each, don't just list them.

questions.question: Debouncing vs Throttling
questions.answer: Debounce: waits until function stops being called for N ms, then fires once. Throttle: fires at most once per N ms interval regardless of how many times called.

use_cases.debounce: Search input, window resize handler, form validation
use_cases.throttle: Scroll event, mousemove, API rate limiting

questions.question: Find the maximum number in an array using JavaScript
questions.tip: Mention Math.max(...arr) can cause stack overflow for very large arrays; reduce is safer.

questions.question: Find the occurrence/frequency of elements in an array
Rest and Spread operators
questions.answer: Same syntax (...), opposite intent. Spread expands an iterable into individual elements. Rest collects remaining arguments into an array.

questions.question: How do you prevent XSS in a form input?
questions.answer: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) = injecting malicious scripts into a page via user input.
prevention: Sanitize input - strip or encode HTML tags. Use DOMPurify for rich text.
React escapes JSX values by default - never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user input.
Validate on backend - client-side validation is not enough.
Encode output - encode < > " ' & when rendering user content.
Set CSP header - restricts which scripts can run.
HttpOnly cookies - XSS can't steal tokens if stored in HttpOnly cookies.

questions.question: What is a Content Security Policy (CSP) header and why does it matter?
questions.answer: CSP is an HTTP response header that tells the browser which sources are trusted for scripts, styles, images etc. It's the last line of defense against XSS.
questions.tip: Mention nonce-based CSP for dynamic scripts - each script tag gets a random nonce value matching the header.

questions.question: Difference between display: inline, inline-block, and block
questions.answer: block: full width, stacks vertically, respects width/height/margin. inline: flows with text, only content width, ignores width/height/vertical margin. inline-block: flows inline but respects all box model properties.

examples.inline-block: buttons, badges - flows in text but has dimensions

questions.question: Product search page - state structure before writing any code
questions.answer: The interviewer watches how you structure state before writing any code. Keep state minimal - derive everything you can.
questions.tip: State should be minimal. If something can be computed from existing state, derive it - don't store it.

questions.question: Debounced search input - no useEffect mistakes
questions.answer: Use a separate debouncedQuery state updated by useEffect with cleanup to avoid memory leaks.
common_mistakes: Fetching inside the input onChange directly
Infinite loop: putting fetch result in state that's in the dependency array

questions.question: Build infinite scroll - handle 10,000 items without freezing the UI
questions.answer: Combine list virtualization, debounced scroll, and API pagination.
techniques: List virtualization - only render visible rows (react-window or react-virtual). DOM has ~20 nodes instead of 10,000.
Debounce scroll handler - don't fire on every pixel scroll
API pagination - load 20 items at a time using Intersection Observer
questions.tip: Mention layout thrash: happens when you read and write DOM in the same frame. Batch reads/writes or use requestAnimationFrame.

questions.question: What causes layout thrash and how do you fix it?
questions.answer: Layout thrash = reading layout properties (offsetHeight, clientWidth) then immediately writing DOM styles, forcing the browser to recalculate layout repeatedly.
questions.tip: Use requestAnimationFrame to batch DOM writes before the next paint.

questions.question: React Reconciliation and React Fiber
questions.answer: Reconciliation is React's algorithm to diff old and new virtual DOM trees and compute minimal real DOM changes. React Fiber (React 16+) reimplemented reconciliation to support interruptible, priority-based rendering.
key_points: Reconciliation: same component type = update, different type = unmount/remount
Fiber: work is broken into small units - can pause, resume, abort
Enables Concurrent Mode: React works on updates in background without blocking UI
Priority-based scheduling: urgent updates (user input) interrupt lower-priority ones
questions.tip: Mention useTransition and useDeferredValue as APIs that expose concurrent features to app code.

questions.question: Virtual DOM and its benefits
questions.answer: The Virtual DOM is a lightweight JS object representation of the real DOM. On state change, React creates a new VDOM tree, diffs it (reconciliation), and applies only the changed parts to the real DOM.
benefits: Declarative code - describe what, not how
Cross-platform - same VDOM concept for React Native
questions.tip: Be ready for: 'Is Virtual DOM always faster?' - No. For small/static pages, direct DOM manipulation can be faster. VDOM shines at scale.

questions.question: Application optimization techniques in React
techniques: React.memo - skip re-render if props haven't changed
Code splitting - React.lazy + Suspense to load routes on demand
Avoid context re-renders - split contexts, or use Zustand/Jotai for fine-grained updates
Lazy state initialization - pass a function to useState for expensive initial values
Always measure in production mode - dev mode adds overhead

questions.question: What is a bundler and how does it work?
questions.answer: A bundler (Webpack, Vite, Parcel, esbuild) takes JS modules and dependencies and combines them into optimized files for the browser.
questions.tip: Vite uses native ES modules in dev (no bundling, ultra-fast HMR) and Rollup for production builds.

questions.question: Walk me through a frontend bug you fixed in production
questions.answer: Use STAR format: Situation → Task → Action → Result. Focus on your debugging process, not just the fix.
questions.template: We had a production issue where [describe symptom]. I was responsible for [your role]. I identified the root cause by [how: logs, repro, devtools]. The fix was [specific change]. We prevented recurrence by [monitoring/tests added].
good_examples: Memory leak from uncleared event listeners
questions.tip: Mention tools: Chrome DevTools, React DevTools, Sentry, Lighthouse.

questions.question: How do you decide when to refactor vs ship?
questions.answer: Consider business context and impact, not just technical purity.

ship_if: Refactor scope is large and can be isolated
refactor_if: Code is a known bug source
framework.best_approach: Boy scout rule - leave code slightly better than you found it. Refactor incrementally, not in big-bang rewrites.

questions.question: Your team disagrees on an approach. What do you do?
questions.answer: Show intellectual humility + decisiveness + team-first thinking.
questions.strong_answer: I'd first make sure I understand their reasoning fully. Then I'd present my perspective with data/tradeoffs, not just opinion. If we can't align, I'd suggest a time-boxed spike or proof-of-concept to let the code decide. Ultimately, I can 'disagree and commit' once a decision is made - the team moving together matters more than being right.

questions.question: Design a component library for a fintech product at scale
questions.answer: Cover design tokens, accessibility, API design, versioning, docs, testing, and performance.

areas.tokens: Design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) as the foundation. Single source of truth.
areas.accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, keyboard navigation, ARIA roles. Non-negotiable for fintech.
areas.api_design: Composable, prop-based. Avoid tightly coupled components.
areas.versioning: Semantic versioning, changelog. Breaking changes are major versions.
areas.docs: Storybook - interactive playground for every component.
areas.testing: Unit tests (Jest), visual regression (Chromatic/Percy), interaction tests (Testing Library).
areas.performance: Tree-shakeable exports, lazy loading for heavy components.

questions.tip: Mention that PhonePe handles payments - security, trust indicators, and error states must be first-class citizens.

questions.question: How do you debug a performance issue in production?
steps: Reproduce locally - Chrome DevTools Performance tab, find long tasks
Check Core Web Vitals - LCP, FID/INP, CLS, Time to Interactive
Network tab - large bundles, blocking resources, waterfall issues
React DevTools Profiler - find unnecessary re-renders
Real User Monitoring - Sentry, Datadog for real-world impact confirmation

questions.question: What would you redesign on Myntra's product listing page and why?
questions.answer: Use the Myntra app before this round. The redesign question is specific to their product.
framework: Identify a real pain point you noticed while using the app
Frame it as: current state → user problem → proposed solution → measurable impact
Consider: filter UX, image loading, scroll performance, search relevance, mobile experience
questions.tip: Use the Myntra app before this round. That redesign question is specific to their product.

questions.question: Why Myntra over other product companies?
questions.answer: Fashion tech at this scale is a specific problem. Show you understand it.
tips: Mention scale: millions of SKUs, high-res images, real-time inventory
Talk about unique frontend challenges: virtual try-on, personalization, seasonal traffic spikes
Reference something specific from Myntra's tech blog or product
